Many letters of the [[Latin alphabet]], both capital and small, are used in [[mathematics]], [[science]], and [[engineering]] to denote by convention specific or abstracted constants, variables of a certain type, units, multipliers, or physical entities. Certain letters, when combined with special formatting, take on special meaning.

Below is an alphabetical list of the letters of the alphabet with some of their uses. The field in which the convention applies is mathematics unless otherwise noted.

==Typographical variation==

Some common conventions:
* Most symbols are written in [[Italic type|italic]]s.
* [[Vector (geometry)|Vector]]s can be denoted in [[boldface]]. 
* Sets of [[number]]s are typically bold or [[blackboard bold]].

==Aa==
* A represents:
** the first point of a [[triangle]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Triangle |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Triangle.html |access-date=2022-03-21 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
** the digit "ten" in [[hexadecimal]]<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Hexadecimal - Hexadecimal and character sets - GCSE Computer Science Revision |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize/guides/zp73wmn/revision/1 |access-date=2022-03-21 |website=BBC Bitesize |language=en-GB}}</ref> and other positional numeral systems with a radix of 11 or greater<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=DECIMAL function |url=https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/decimal-function-ee554665-6176-46ef-82de-0a283658da2e#:~:text=A%20radix%20greater%20than%2010,#NUM!%20or%20#VALUE! |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=support.microsoft.com}}</ref>
** the unit [[ampere]] for electric current in [[physics]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-10-07 |title=BIPM - SI base units |url=http://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/section2-1.html |website=bipm.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141007203046/http://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/section2-1.html |archive-date=2014-10-07}}</ref>
** the [[area]] of a figure<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2014-10-07 |title=BIPM - SI derived units |url=http://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/section2-2.html |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=bipm.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141007193455/http://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure/section2-2.html |archive-date=2014-10-07}}</ref>
** the [[mass number]] or [[Mass number|nucleon number]] of an element in [[chemistry]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jensen |first=William B. |date=December 2005 |title=The Origins of the Symbols A and Z for Atomic Weight and Number |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ed082p1764 |journal=Journal of Chemical Education |language=en |volume=82 |issue=12 |pages=1764 |doi=10.1021/ed082p1764 |bibcode=2005JChEd..82.1764J |issn=0021-9584|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
** the [[Helmholtz free energy]] of a closed thermodynamic system of constant pressure and temperature<ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-06-21 |title=22.1: Helmholtz Energy |url=https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Physical_and_Theoretical_Chemistry_Textbook_Maps/Physical_Chemistry_(LibreTexts)/22%3A_Helmholtz_and_Gibbs_Energies/22.01%3A_Helmholtz_Energy |access-date=2022-03-23 |website=Chemistry LibreTexts |language=en}}</ref>
** a [[vector potential]], in electromagnetics it can refer to the [[magnetic vector potential]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=The magnetic vector potential |url=https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/em/lectures/node38.html |access-date=2022-03-21 |website=farside.ph.utexas.edu}}</ref>
** with a subscript, an [[alternating group]] on that many objects
** an [[Abelian group]] in abstract algebra
** the [[Glaisher–Kinkelin constant]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Glaisher-Kinkelin Constant |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Glaisher-KinkelinConstant.html |access-date=2022-03-21 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
** [[Atomic Weight|atomic weight]], denoted by ''A''<sub>r</sub> <ref name=":6" />
** [[Work (physics)|work]] in [[classical mechanics]]<ref name=":6" />
** the [[pre-exponential factor]]<ref name=":6" /> in the [[Arrhenius equation|Arrhenius Equation]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-10-02 |title=6.2.3.1: Arrhenius Equation |url=https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Physical_and_Theoretical_Chemistry_Textbook_Maps/Supplemental_Modules_(Physical_and_Theoretical_Chemistry)/Kinetics/06%3A_Modeling_Reaction_Kinetics/6.02%3A_Temperature_Dependence_of_Reaction_Rates/6.2.03%3A_The_Arrhenius_Law/6.2.3.01%3A_Arrhenius_Equation |access-date=2022-04-03 |website=Chemistry LibreTexts |language=en}}</ref>
** [[electron affinity]]<ref name=":6" />
** A [[blood type]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blood Types |url=https://stanfordbloodcenter.org/donate-blood/blood-donation-facts/blood-types/ |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=Stanford Blood Center |language=en-US}}</ref>
*<math>\mathbb{A}</math> represents the [[algebraic numbers]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Algebraic Number |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/AlgebraicNumber.html |access-date=2022-03-22 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref> or affine space in [[Algebraic Geometry|algebraic geometry]].
** A [[spectral type]]
* a represents:
** the first side of a triangle (opposite point A)<ref name=":0" />
** the [[Scale factor (Universe)|scale factor]] of the expanding universe in [[cosmology]]<ref>{{Cite book |last=Liebscher |first=Dierck-Ekkehard |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VK_rbBR61eUC&pg=PA53 |title=Cosmology |publisher=Springer |year=2005 |isbn=9783540232612 |location=Berlin |pages=53–77 |language=}}</ref>
** the [[acceleration]] in [[Equations of motion|mechanics equations]]<ref name=":1" />
** the first constant in a [[linear equation]]
** a constant in a [[polynomial]]
** the unit [[Hectare#Are|are]] for area (100 m<sup>2</sup>)<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |title=Conversion factors and tables. Part 1. Basis of tables. Conversion factors. |date=1974 |publisher=BSI |others=British Standards Institution |isbn=0-580-08471-X |edition=3rd revision |location=London |pages=7 |oclc=32212391}}</ref>
**the unit prefix [[Atto-|atto]] (10<sup>−18</sup>)<ref>{{Cite book |title=Conversion factors and tables. Part 1. Basis of tables. Conversion factors. |date=1974 |publisher=BSI |others=British Standards Institution |isbn=0-580-08471-X |edition=3rd revision |location=London |pages=4 |oclc=32212391}}</ref>
**the first term in a [[sequence]] or [[Series (mathematics)|series]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arithmetic Progression - Formula, Examples {{!}} AP Formula |url=https://www.cuemath.com/algebra/arithmetic-progressions/ |access-date=2022-03-24 |website=Cuemath |language=en}}</ref>
** [[Reflectance]]

==Bb==
*B represents:
**the digit "11" in [[hexadecimal]]<ref name=":3" /> and other positional numeral systems with a radix of 12 or greater<ref name=":4" />
**the second point of a triangle<ref name=":0" />
**a [[Ball (mathematics)|ball]] (also denoted by ℬ (<math>\mathcal{B}</math>) or <math>\mathbb{B}</math>)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Ball |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Ball.html |access-date=2022-03-24 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>
** a [[basis (linear algebra)|basis]] of a vector space or of a [[filter (mathematics)|filter]] (both also denoted by ℬ (<math>\mathcal{B}</math>))
** in econometrics and time-series statistics it is often used for the backshift or [[lag operator]], the formal parameter of the lag polynomial
**the [[magnetic field]], denoted <math>\textbf{B}</math> or <math>\vec{B}</math>
*''B'' with various [[subscript]]s represents several variations of [[Brun's constant]] and [[Betti number]]s; it can also be used to mean the [[Bernoulli number]]s.
** [[B meson]]
** A [[blood type]]
** [[Boron]]
** [[Buoyancy]]
** [[Bulk modulus]]
** [[Luminance]]
** A [[spectral type]]
*b represents:
**the second side of a triangle (opposite point B)
**the [[impact parameter]] in nuclear [[scattering]]
**the second constant in a [[linear equation]]
**usually with an index, sometimes with an arrow over it, a [[basis vector]]
**a [[breadth]]<ref name=":6" />
**the [[molality]] of a solution<ref name=":6" />
** [[Standard Model|Bottom quark]]
** [[Barn (unit)|Barn]] ({{math|10<sup>−24</sup>}} cm{{math|<sup>2</sup>}})

==Cc==
* C represents:
** the third point of a triangle
** the digit "12" in [[hexadecimal]] and other positional numeral systems with a radix of 13 or greater
** the unit [[coulomb]] of electrical charge<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last1=Stohner |first1=Jürgen |last2=Quack |first2=Martin |date=2011 |title=A Concise Summary of Quantities, Units, and Symbols in Physical Chemistry |url=http://publications.iupac.org/ci/2011/3304/July11_green-sup-4p.pdf |journal=Chemistry International |publisher=[[De Gruyter]] |volume=33 |issue=4 |pages=Centerfold |no-pp=y}}</ref>
** [[capacitance]] in electrical theory
** with indices denoting the number of combinations, a binomial coefficient
** together with a degree symbol (°), the [[Celsius]] measurement of temperature = °C<ref name=":6" />
** the [[circumference]] of a circle or other closed curve<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Circumference |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Circumference.html |access-date=2025-02-01 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en |quote=In the work, the term "circumference" is used to mean the perimeter of a circle. However, some authors allow "circumference" to refer more generally to the distance or arc length around an arbitrary closed object (sometimes restricted to a closed plane figure such as a lamina).}}</ref>
** with a subscript, a [[cycle (graph theory)|cycle]] on that many vertices
** with a subscript, a [[cyclic group]] of that order
** the [[Complement (set theory)|complement]] of a set (lowercase ''c'' and the symbol ∁ are also used)
** an arbitrary [[category (mathematics)|category]]
** the [[number concentration]]<ref name=":6" />*
** [[Carbon]]
** [[Heat capacity]]
** The [[C (programming language)|C programming language]]
** [[Cunningham correction factor]]
* <math>\mathbb{C}</math> represents the [[Set (mathematics)|set]] of [[complex numbers]].
* A vertically elongated C with an integer subscript n sometimes denotes the n-th coefficient of a formal [[power series]].
* c represents:
** the unit prefix [[Centi-|centi]] (10<sup>−2</sup>)<ref name=":6" />
** the [[amount concentration]] in chemistry<ref name=":6" />
** the [[speed of light]] in vacuum<ref>{{cite book |last1=Prasad |first1=Paras N. |title=Introduction to Biophotonics |date=16 January 2004 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-0-471-46539-3 |page=12 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zF1GYVamV34C&pg=PA12 |language=en}}</ref>
** the third side of a triangle (opposite corner C)
**the third constant in a [[linear equation]]
**a constant in a [[polynomial]]
** [[Charm quark]]
** [[Speed of sound]]
** [[Specific heat capacity]]
* Lowercase [[Fraktur]] <math>\mathfrak{c}</math> denotes the [[Cardinality of the continuum|cardinality of the set of real numbers]] (the "continuum"), or, equivalently, of the power set of natural numbers.

==Dd==
* D represents 
** the digit "13" in [[hexadecimal]] and other positional numeral systems with a radix of 14 or greater
** [[diffusion]] coefficient or diffusivity in dimensions of [distance<sup>2</sup>/time]
** the [[differential operator]] in Euler's calculus notation
** with a subscript, a [[dihedral group]] of that order or a dihedral group on a regular polygon of that many sides, depending on the convention chosen
** [[Bond-dissociation energy|dissociation energy]]<ref name=":6" />
** [[Dimension]]
** [[Deuterium]]
** [[Electric displacement]]
** [[D meson]]
** [[Density]]
* d represents
** the [[differential operator]]
** the unit day of time (86,400 s)
** the difference in an arithmetic sequence
** a metric operator/function
** the [[diameter]] of a circle<ref name=":6" />
** the unit prefix [[Deci-|deci]] (10<sup>−1</sup>)<ref name=":6" />
** a [[Vertical position|thickness]]<ref name=":6" />
** a [[distance]]<ref name=":6" />
** [[Down quark]]
** [[Infinitesimal]] increment in [[calculus]]
** [[Density]]

==Ee==
*E represents:
**the digit "14" in [[hexadecimal]] and other positional numeral systems with a radix of 15 or greater
**an exponent in decimal numbers. For example, 1.2E3 is 1.2×10<sup>3</sup> or 1200
**the set of edges in a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] or [[matroid]]
**the unit prefix [[exa]] (10<sup>18</sup>)<ref name=":6" />
**[[energy]] in physics<ref name=":6" />
**[[electric field]] denoted <math>\textbf{E}</math> or <math>\vec{E}</math>
** [[electromotive force]] (denoted <math>\mathcal{E}</math> and measured in [[volts]]), refers to [[voltage]]
**an [[event (probability theory)|event]] (as in P('''E'''), which reads "the probability P of event '''E''' occurring")
**in statistics, the [[expected value]] of a random variable, sometimes as <math>\mathbb{E}</math>
**''E''<sub>k</sub> represents [[kinetic energy]]<ref name=":6" />
** ''(''Arrhenius) [[activation energy]], denoted ''E''<sub>a</sub> or ''E''<sub>A</sub><ref name=":6" />
** [[ionization energy]], denoted ''E''<sub>i</sub><ref name=":6" />
** [[electron affinity]], denoted ''E''<sub>ea</sub><ref>{{Cite book |title=Quantities, Units and Symbols in Physical Chemistry |publisher=International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry |year=1993 |isbn=0-632-03583-8 |pages=20 |language=En}}</ref>
** [[Bond-dissociation energy|dissociation energy]], denoted ''E''<sub>d</sub><ref name=":6" />
*e represents:
**[[e (mathematical constant)|Euler's number]], a transcendental number equal to 2.71828182845... which is used as the base for natural logarithms
**a vector of unit length, especially in the direction of one of the coordinates axes
**the [[elementary charge]] in [[physics]]
**an [[electron]], usually denoted e<sup>−</sup> to distinguish against a [[positron]] e<sup>+</sup>
**the [[eccentricity (geometry)|eccentricity]] of a conic section
**the identity element in a [[Group (mathematics)|group]]
** In a [[cartesian coordinate system]], a [[unit vector]] in notations like <math alt="e-hat sub x, e-hat sub y, e-hat sub z">(\mathbf{\hat{e}}_x, \mathbf{\hat{e}}_y, \mathbf{\hat{e}}_z)</math>, or <math alt= "e-hat sub 1, e-hat sub 2, e-hat sub 3">(\mathbf{\hat{e}}_1, \mathbf{\hat{e}}_2, \mathbf{\hat{e}}_3)</math>

==Ff==
*F represents
**the digit "15" in [[hexadecimal]] and other positional numeral systems with a radix of 16 or greater
**the unit [[farad]] of electrical capacity<ref name=":6" />
**the [[Helmholtz free energy]] of a closed thermodynamic system of constant pressure and temperature
** together with a degree symbol (°) represents the [[Fahrenheit]] measurement of temperature = °F
** [[Fluorine]]
** A [[spectral type]]
*''F'' represents
**[[force]] in mechanics equations<ref name=":6" />
**''<sub>p</sub>F<sub>q</sub>'' is a [[hypergeometric series]]
**the [[probability distribution]] [[function (mathematics)|function]] in [[statistics]]
**a [[Fibonacci number]]
** an arbitrary [[functor (category theory)|functor]]
** a [[field (mathematics)|field]]
** an [[event space]] sigma algebra as part of a probability space, often as <math>\mathcal{F}</math>
*f represents:
**the unit prefix [[femto]] (10<sup>−15</sup>)<ref name=":6" />
*''f'' represents:
**the generic designation of a [[function (mathematics)|function]]
** [[Friction]]

==Gg==
*G represents
**an arbitrary [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]], as in: ''G''(''V'',''E'')
**an arbitrary [[group (mathematics)|group]]
**the unit prefix [[giga]] (10<sup>9</sup>)<ref name=":6" />
**the [[Newtonian constant of gravitation]]<ref name=":6" />
**the [[Einstein tensor]]
**the [[Gibbs energy]]
**the [[centroid]] of a triangle
**[[Catalan's constant]]
**[[weight]] measured in [[Newton (unit)|newtons]]<ref name=":6" />
** [[Green's function]]
** a [[spectral type]]
*g represents:
**the generic designation of a second function
**the acceleration due to [[Free fall|gravity on Earth]]
**a unit of mass, the [[gram]] (also ''gramme'')
** [[Gravitational field]], denoted '''g'''
** [[Metric tensor (general relativity)]]
** [[Gluon]]

==Hh==
*H represents:
** an arbitrary subgraph
** an arbitrary subgroup
** a [[Hilbert space]]
** the unit [[henry (unit)|henry]] of magnetic inductance<ref name=":6" />
** the [[homology (mathematics)|homology]] and [[cohomology]] [[functor]]
** the [[enthalpy]]
** the (Shannon) [[entropy (information theory)|entropy of information]]
** the [[orthocenter]] of a triangle
** a partial sum of the [[harmonic series (mathematics)|harmonic series]]
** [[Auxiliary magnetic field]], denoted <math>\boldsymbol{H}</math>
** [[Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)|Hamiltonian in quantum mechanics]]
** [[Hankel function]]
** [[Heaviside step function]]
** [[Higgs boson]]
** [[Hydrogen]]
** Set of [[quaternion]]s
** [[Hat matrix]]
*H<sub>0</sub> is either the [[Hubble constant]]; or the [[Dimensionless Hubble parameter]] of (100 h km·[[second|s]]<sup>−1</sup>·[[megaparsec|Mpc]]<sup>−1</sup>, with h being the associated error.
*<math>\mathbb{H}</math> represents the [[quaternion]]s (after [[William Rowan Hamilton]]).
*ΔH<sup>‡</sup> represents the standard [[enthalpy of activation]]<ref name=":6" /> in the [[Eyring equation]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-10-02 |title=6.4.1: Eyring equation |url=https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Physical_and_Theoretical_Chemistry_Textbook_Maps/Supplemental_Modules_(Physical_and_Theoretical_Chemistry)/Kinetics/06%3A_Modeling_Reaction_Kinetics/6.04%3A_Transition_State_Theory/6.4.01%3A_Eyring_equation |access-date=2022-04-03 |website=Chemistry LibreTexts |language=en}}</ref>
*ℋ (<math>\mathcal{H}</math>) represents the Hamiltonian in [[Hamiltonian mechanics]].
*h represents:
**the [[class number (number theory)|class number]] in [[algebraic number theory]]
**a small increment in the argument of a function
**the unit [[hour]] for [[time]] (3600 s)
**the [[Planck constant]] (6.626 069(57)× 10<sup>−34</sup> J·s)
**the unit prefix [[hecto]] (10{{sup|2}})<ref name=":6" />
**the generic designation of a third function
**the [[altitude (geometry)|altitude]] of a triangle
**a [[height]]<ref name=":6" />
** [[Spherical Hankel function]]

==Ii==
*I represents:
**the closed unit interval, which contains all real numbers from 0 to 1, inclusive
**the [[identity matrix]]
**the [[Irradiance]]
